hero.title_html: Know where you stand before the day you need to.
hero.lede: Shield Point Strategies helps schools, churches, businesses and public agencies get honest about their risks, plan for the worst day, and train the people who will be there when it comes — led by a police chief of twenty years.

layers.name: Deter
layers.short: Make it obvious this place is ready.
layers.text: Lighting, sightlines, visible controls, posture and presence. Most trouble goes where it is easiest; the first layer makes sure that is not here.
layers.we: Site walk, perimeter and entry review, visitor-management recommendations.

layers.name: Detect
layers.short: See it early, from where you are.
layers.text: Cameras that are watched, alarms that mean something, staff who know what unusual looks like and have a way to say so.
layers.we: Camera and alarm coverage review, reporting pathways, threat-assessment team setup.

layers.name: Delay
layers.text: Controlled entries, locked classrooms and offices, interior doors that hold, a building that slows a threat long enough for people to move and responders to arrive.
layers.we: Access-control and door-hardware review, secure-entry design, lockdown procedures.

layers.name: Respond
layers.text: A plan people have actually practiced. Who calls, who moves, who locks, who talks to the responders, and how it all gets communicated in the first ninety seconds.
layers.we: Emergency operations plans, drills and tabletop exercises, staff training, law-enforcement coordination.

layers.name: Recover
layers.short: Get back to normal, on purpose.
layers.text: Reunification, communication with families and the public, support for the people involved, and an honest look at what to change.
layers.we: Reunification planning, after-action review, continuity planning.

services_intro.title: What we do
services_intro.lede: Three words on the shield, three kinds of work. Every engagement starts with a conversation and a walk through your building.

services.name: Security & Safety Assessments
services.short: A full walk of your site with a chief's eyes, and a written report you can act on.
body: We walk your property the way someone looking for a weakness would, then the way a first responder would arrive. Entries, sightlines, lighting, locks, cameras, visitor flow, where people gather and how they would get out.
You get a plain-language report ranked by what matters most, not a sales sheet for equipment. Most of what we recommend costs little or nothing.
points: Schools, churches, offices, retail, clinics and public buildings

services.name: Emergency Operations Planning
services.short: Plans people can run from memory, built for your building and your people.
body: A plan that lives in a binder nobody has opened is not a plan. We build emergency operations plans for the events that are actually likely where you are — intruder, fire, medical, weather, utility failure, a threat made online — and keep them short enough to use.
Then we test them with your team, on paper and on your feet, until the plan matches the building.
points: Emergency operations plans and lockdown procedures
Coordination with local police, fire and dispatch

services.name: Training
services.short: For staff, leadership, boards and volunteers — what to notice, what to do, what to say.
body: Most people freeze because nobody ever told them what their job is on a bad day. We teach it in plain terms: situational awareness, recognizing concerning behavior, de-escalation, what to do in the first minute of an emergency, and how to work with responders when they arrive.
Sessions are built for your audience — teachers, ushers, front-desk staff, managers, boards — and fit into a staff meeting or a half day.
points: Emergency response for staff and volunteers

services.name: Law Enforcement & Public-Agency Consulting
services.short: Twenty years running a department, offered to yours.
body: Policy review, leadership development, program design, community-policing strategy, emergency-communications planning and the hundred practical questions of running a small agency well.

Chief Asmus built the Liberty Lake Police Department from its founding and sits on the regional emergency-communications board. If you are standing up a program, reviewing one, or preparing for an assessment, that experience is available to you.
points: Preparation for accreditation and outside review

steps.name: A conversation
steps.text: What worries you, what has happened, what you have in place. Thirty minutes, no charge.

steps.name: The walk
steps.text: We walk your site with you, inside and out, and talk to the people who are there every day.

steps.name: The plan
steps.text: A written report and, where you want it, the plans and training to close the gaps.

steps.name: The practice
steps.text: Drills and tabletop exercises on a schedule that fits you, and a check-in when things change.

readiness.title: The readiness check
readiness.lede: Ten honest questions. Two minutes. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose to send it.

questions.q: Can a visitor walk into your building without passing a person or a locked door?
Is the outside of your building lit at night, with clear sightlines to every entrance?
If a camera caught something right now, would anyone see it within a minute?
Do your staff have a simple way to report something that feels wrong — and know it will be taken seriously?
Can every room where people gather be locked from the inside, quickly, without a key hunt?
Are there doors that get propped open during the day?
Has your team run a drill — any drill — in the last twelve months?
Does every staff member know who calls 911, who locks down, and who talks to responders?
If you had to evacuate, do you have a written plan for reuniting people with their families?
After your last incident or close call, did anyone write down what to change?

readings.title: Start with the walk.
readings.text: There are real gaps here, and most of them are fixable without buying anything. The right first step is a site walk and a ranked list.

readings.title: Good bones, thin in places.
readings.text: You have the basics. The layers that scored low are where the next incident will find you — let's close those first.

readings.title: Well prepared. Keep it sharp.
readings.text: You are ahead of most. The work now is practice: drills, a tabletop exercise, and a second set of eyes on the plan.

faqs.q: Do you only work with schools?
faqs.a: No. Schools are a large part of the work, but the same layers protect a church on Sunday, a clinic lobby, a small office or a city building. If people gather there, we can help.

faqs.q: Are you going to tell us to buy a lot of equipment?
faqs.a: No. Most findings are about doors, habits, sightlines and who knows what. Where equipment genuinely helps, we say so and tell you what matters and what does not.
It depends on the size of the site and what you need after the walk. The first conversation is free; after that you get a clear quote before any work starts. Ask us.
We are based in Liberty Lake, Washington and work across the Inland Northwest. For work farther out, ask — it often works.

contact.title: Start with a conversation
contact.lede: Tell us what you are responsible for and what worries you. We will come back to you directly — no sales team, no form that disappears.
